lines: Try five new animated villager appearances from the debug menu.
Penguin, white tiger, lion, robin and raccoon use the existing 128px texture resolution.
Select one villager and apply an unused appearance without changing their name, jobs or location.
Visual changes last for the current session; existing save species and resident identities remain stable.
Prepare short-code GameCube linking for staging builds.
Device credentials are scoped and revocable, and checkpoint uploads can resume.
Staging supports TLS movement and resumable review of guest placements.
Public GameCube visits still require world sync, save settlement, and hardware qualification.
The multiplayer server can link accounts, import towns, and manage guest admission.
A short code links a GameCube session to a town account on the server.
The first validated town save is kept as a checkpoint for future reconciliation.
Open gates admit two mutual friends and keep disconnected seats for up to one minute.
Find borrowed job items after at most one redirect.
Retrieval errands visit at most two borrowers before returning to the owner.
The second borrower always supplies the item once you have pocket space.
Older saved chains finish at their current borrower and keep their reward tier.
Write letters and attach presents straight from your backpack.
Both writing papers open the letter composer; eligible gifts can be attached.
Cancelling preserves your items and returns to the menu you started from.
Floor, wallpaper and furniture actions respect the current home context.
Load standalone game assets beside the launched DOL.
The updated SDK resolves SD Gecko, SD2SP2 and GC Loader paths.
A moved app folder keeps its own matching assets for the whole session.
Disc startup and bounded discovery for missing launch paths are preserved.
See what's new in each AnimalTown update.
The version file records four lines for each request.
The release combines the new requests into one brief summary.
The published release includes the summary alongside its downloads.
See how much time is left on your update download.
The updater shows the estimated time beneath the progress bar.
The countdown follows recent transfer speed and clears on a stall.
The screen reports verification and restart once the download finishes.
Lay the groundwork for richer villager errands.
Job rules, randomness and cooldown state now have a saved foundation.
The town keeps running while menus pause only the job cooldown clock.
Playable offers, objectives and rewards will follow in later changes.
Document the plan for the complete offline villager errand system.
Fourteen phases cover all twelve job types and four player profiles.
The roadmap includes real mail, rewards and memory-card town travel.
Each phase defines completion checks and resource validation.
Cherry blossom trees bloom during the first ten days of spring.
Their wider, lower canopies distinguish them year-round.
New towns grow cherry trees among their other deciduous trees.
Buy cherry blossom saplings from the essentials cabinet.
Regular deciduous trees have slightly taller canopies.
The top cluster sits higher on a mature tree.
The taller silhouette makes these trees easier to tell apart from cherry blossoms.
The shared tree mesh still uses 84 triangles.
Blooming cherry blossoms now shed little pink petals.
Petals occasionally flutter down from nearby mature trees.
Cherry canopies extend down over the top of the trunk.
Regular deciduous canopies reach a little higher.
Cherry blossoms blend base pink with lighter blush and darker rose.
Soft color patches follow the shapes of the canopy clusters.
The pattern uses the trees' existing noise.
The effect uses the shared tree mesh and texture.
Choose a season or time of day to preview in the debug menu.
Left and Right browse season choices and A loads the selected season.
The time preview holds weather and outdoor lighting at the selected time.
Panel titles stay still.
Chat as your villager using the controller keyboard.
Open Chat in Settings or press R while playing.
With debug menus visible, /attend name text makes that neighbour call out.
Long messages wrap into pages; ordinary chat shows your own name.
Snow rolls in once a day in winter, at a random time for each town.
Each snowfall lasts from 30 minutes to three hours.
If it snows while you're away, your town's snow is smooth when you return.
All villagers share the same snowfall and snow dents, and paths are unaffected.
Add resident errands, real letters and two-card town travel.
Keep offers, unique parcels, progress and earned rewards across sessions.
Connect physical world favors, outfits, room rewards and opening employment.
Preserve four resident profiles with a separate visitor and recoverable card handoffs.
Keep saved snow and resident job progress together after updating.
Read older snowfall saves and earlier resident-job preview saves.
Preserve parcels, profiles and partially recovered snow across reloads.
Keep unchanged saves and independent snow or job-clock updates efficient.
Find villager houses, the store, and the helipad with the new town map legend.
Each villager house has a permanent marker on the map.
The legend distinguishes villager houses from moving villagers.
It also identifies player homes, the post office, and your current location.
Take a helicopter from the north helipad to another town.
Board from the grass in front of the pad during a two-card visit.
Fly across the sky while the destination is loading.
Land beside the destination gate and walk straight into town.
Compare optional terrain prefetch and record performance without the overlay.
A saved debug toggle enables bounded asynchronous terrain lookahead.
Profiling offers counters, video telemetry and a small rolling capture.
Memory ownership, peak usage and transfer waits are available for diagnosis.
Each playable villager gets a separate memory-card entry.
The entry is labeled by villager slot and uses its own card blocks.
An explicit save moves existing villagers out of the shared town entry.
Deleting a villager in the game frees that villager's entry.
Video and debug settings each get a separate memory-card entry.
Each settings entry uses one block.
Existing settings move when you save them or save your town with enough free space.
Deleting a town in the game preserves both settings entries.
The north helipad has a flat timber surface with a painted landing mark.
The plank seams, cream H, and corner marks are drawn with color polygons.
The helicopter now sits level with the pad when parked.
A windsock still marks the landing area.
The minimap fades in after two seconds of running.
The minimap fades out after four seconds without running.
The date and time fade out when you run and return when you stop.
Each fade takes about a quarter of a second.
Two-card travel can save progress without moving older save files.
The game rechecks the selected town card before writing.
Optional card-layout cleanup runs during regular saves.
Card errors identify the slot and operation that failed.
Store menus keep the left half of the shop in view.
Buying, selling, and consignment use compact panels on the right.
Failed placement, planting, dropping, and burial explain what blocked the action.
Cherry blossom trees have taller crowns and petals fall from higher up.
Bunny, giraffe, hamster and Maine coon villagers have updated animated models.
The new models include walking and running animations.
Their textures fit within 128 by 128 pixels.
Existing saves keep the same villager species.
Bunny, giraffe, hamster and Maine coon villagers animate while standing still.
The new idle clips play for both players and residents.
Walking and running take over when a villager moves.
Idle clips use compact keyframes to fit GameCube memory.
Shop menus show GameCube button glyphs beside their actions.
Green A marks available actions such as buying and selling.
Red B marks the back or close action.
Sold-out displays and empty pockets show the close prompt.
Kick up autumn leaves while walking normally or running.
Running uses the same three-leaf footstep effect as normal walking.
Gentle movement below half walking speed emits no new leaves.
The effect reuses its existing atlas and bounded particle buffer.
Visit the new koban to collect lost property and restore visitor removals.
Visitors can add or change town items; removed items stay in the town's lost and found.
Only local human residents can collect property; shop purchases remain permanent.
Save migrations preserve old towns, and authenticated item operations protect custody.
Write letters and town notices with the same QWERTY keyboard and controls as chat.
Use A to type, X to erase, L for case and R for spaces; NL keeps multiline letters.
Drafts retain 1,000 characters, present selection and send or discard confirmations.
Keyboard position and case stay intact while choosing gifts or returning to a draft.
Release CI now shows separate Tests, Build, and Release stages.
Dolphin tests run against the same console image that gets packaged.
Build prepares the backend and release files after the tests pass.
Release checks the prepared files and uploads them to GitHub.
Adjacent snow cutouts now connect into continuous tracks.
Straight tracks, bends and patches keep rounded ends and shaded rims.
As snowfall refills a tile, its joins narrow and close.
The joins reuse the existing winter snow mask.
Snowfall fills deep tracks in one minute and leaves shallow impressions.
Each dent refills to the first indentation level during active snowfall.
Starting play or arriving from another town restores a fresh snow surface.
Outdoor recovery continues while a player is indoors.
Preview smoother snow tracks in Debug / testing.
Footprints ease into their next depth as you cross a tile.
Active snowfall gradually narrows nearby tracks over one minute.
The preview starts off each session and uses the existing snow texture.
Up to two saved characters from the other memory card can visit your town.
The player, five residents, and visiting characters start in separate areas in new towns.
Villager routines and jobs favor places with fewer people nearby.
Visiting characters use their saved appearance and follow local routines.
Winter towns use less memory while keeping the same snow tracks and lighting.
Snow textures cover the visible terrain at their original detail and can unload indoors.
Static shadow data takes less space while keeping the same textures on screen.
The Smooth snow transitions debug setting now applies during play.
NPC visitors come from the other memory card, while player villagers travel under live control.
Up to two saved NPC villagers can join a town when the local player is at the controls.
A player travelling from the other town leaves room for one visiting NPC.
Visiting NPCs follow town routines and use the appearance saved on their own card.
See sandy riverbeds and scattered stones beneath clear turquoise water.
Fine moving ripples, subtle caustics and broken shoreline foam bring shallow water to life.
Archived riverbeds and rocks preserve water levels, bridge traversal and saved towns.
Optional authored water textures replace built-in patterns through the existing asset cooker.
Water previews leave room for town terrain to reload.
Villager model loading follows the preview camera before and after drawing.
Villagers visible only from the saved player position can stay unloaded.
Leaving the preview restores normal camera demand without moving the player.
Resident villagers briefly yield when two others are headed through the same crossing.
Villagers favor outings with fewer residents in or approaching the destination.
A villager can continue after a short wait if a path stays busy.
Visiting villagers follow their own routes and still use ordinary movement collision.
Reduce hidden visual work and release unused world resources.
Indoor terrain and unused room assets return memory automatically.
Snow coverage, distant animation and useful model LODs avoid extra drawing.
Shared memory admission protects active scenes and doorway restoration.
See moving highlights and gentle riverbed refraction on clear inland water.
Two independent wave slopes shape sunlight glints and a restrained environment sheen.
Refraction captures submerged scenery before bridges, dry rocks and villagers are drawn.
Optional slope artwork and a complete technical handoff accompany bounded native rendering.
Avoid idle lighting work and unnecessary visual allocations.
Reuse exact cloud samples and unchanged light projections.
Only drawable terrain requests path resources.
Optional water effects yield memory to required scene restores.
Snow tracks now smooth out over seven minutes of falling snow.
Smooth snow transitions are always enabled.
Productive waits and frame-clear reuse are always enabled too.
The three retired toggles no longer appear in debug menus.
Snow slopes gently down to paths, object footprints and clear-ground patches.
Short white ramps join the raised snow to the original ground.
Snow updates and working buffers exist only during winter.
Leaving winter releases snow meshes, masks, recovery data and memory reservations.
Water effects recover when enough memory becomes available.
Brief pressure no longer leaves affordable water effects permanently suspended.
Required town loads still take priority and retain their memory reservations.
The compact capture resumes only after stable headroom returns.
Water rendering checks reliably reach the coast after terrain loads.
Each inspection shortcut waits for an actual draw from its new camera.
Delayed terrain loading cannot silently consume the next shortcut.
Water animation, refraction and image acceptance remain unchanged.
Free unused terrain and villager memory during play.
Baking returns unused terrain blocks to the ARAM allocator.
Terrain archives can span smaller free blocks during a rebuild.
A restored villager model releases its redundant ARAM copy.
Regular GameCube play keeps its memory available for town loading.
Staging builds can enable short-code pairing for DOL-015 testing.
The standard ISO and Depot app omit the inactive TLS stack.
Pairing builds include both native networking license notices.
Saved towns have more room to load their villager models.
The backpack icon atlas loads after villager models finish loading.
Menus still have their icons when the town opens.
The memory safety margin still applies during villager loading.
Development builds run checks for the features that changed.
The validation plan selects specific Dolphin scenarios and resource fixtures.
Test-only PRs can run host checks without building or publishing a console package.
Full validation and all checks needed to verify release artifacts remain available.
Document the remaining online multiplayer implementation plan.
The Codex brief indexes server authority, transport, NAT and relay work.
It defines visitor custody, owner keep or undo, permanent purchases and safe save handoff.
File mappings, contracts, implementation phases and acceptance checks guide future changes.
Choose smaller home plots and clear only trees that obstruct construction.
Start with a seven-by-five garden and check additional land when expanding.
Terrain, paths, structures, flowers and other belongings stay protected.
Garden reservations and reversible home previews preserve shared-town saves.
Save edge smoothing with normal video preferences, enabled by default.
The former debug antialiasing option is retired from both debug menus.
Existing saved choices migrate without changing town progress.
Versioned settings preserve old cards and protect interrupted migrations.
Preview your actual home plot and control edge smoothing in Video options.
Placement borders, site search and relocation feedback follow the current garden size.
Garden construction explains blockers, and the video toggle saves only applied display changes.
Dolphin checks cover smoothing, restart, deletion controls and protected town records.
Define the internet play PoC for existing towns, guest jobs, chat and resident mail.
The indexed plan reuses backend services and selects local hosting through Cloudflare WSS.
Review resolves offline conflicts; cloned cards, attachments and guest tools stay out of scope.
Dependencies and Dolphin/DOL-015 acceptance gates distinguish planned work from proven behavior.
